subject: Cut points for chest worn device

messages.author: 9f775b86bf12e92f
messages.subject: Cut points for chest worn device
parts:
Dear Vincent, Jairo, and GGIR users,

 

I am a PhD student in Germany and am processing physical activity data from older adults with an average age of 70. The accelerometer was worn on the chest for 7 days during waking hours only. The instrument is Faros 180 and data was recorded at 500 Hz.

In the GGIR cut points guideline from your website Published cut-points and how to use them in GGIR (r-project.org), there are cut-points argument and threshold for wrist and hip worn but unfortunately not for the chest. After reading the previous studies regarding the device attachment site, I could see that the chest worn data was applicable and also highly correlated with the waist worn data.

I was wondering if it would be validable to use the hip worn algorithm built in the GGIR to analyze my chest worn data and what the ideal  argument and threshold  should be for this chest worn data of older adults.

Could you give me some advice on this?

 

Best,

Josua Lim

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Cut points for chest worn device
parts:
Dear Joshua,

I see nobody replied to your question. 

My knowledge of related literature is limited. So, if you are not able to find literature to support using hip-worn cut-points for chest-worn accelerometers then I think this should be done with caution as both can in theory move with different acceleration.

Best,

Vincent
